children: is facing a 2 billion ($2.7 billion) claim in London brought on behalf of app developers over its app tracking rules, filed Thursday at the Competition Appeal Tribunal. The claimants accuse Apple of abusing its position to impose greater restrictions on third parties than on its own services. Apple shares were down 0.35% premarket.

The case centers on App Tracking Transparency, the framework Apple launched in 2021 requiring apps to ask permission before tracking users across other companies' apps and websites. Apple has described the feature as a privacy protection. Lawyers for the claimants argue the requirements fell more heavily on outside developers than on Apple's own advertising business, handing it a competitive advantage. Ann Pope, a former senior antitrust official at the Competition and Markets Authority, is leading the action and said the policy caused "very significant harm to businesses" that rely on Apple as a gatekeeper.
The framework has drawn scrutiny across Europe. Germany's competition authority accused Apple of abusing its market power over the tool, and regulators in France, Italy and Poland have examined it.

title: Apple Faces 2 Billion UK Claim Over App Tracking Rules
